content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "invalid_inference", "fatal": "yes", "explanation": "The quote is verbatim and the objection reads it correctly. \u00a73 proves only that V contains at most one *positive* number (its argument starts \"Suppose V contains two distinct positive numbers c1 > c2 > 0\"). Nothing in the write-up excludes negative values of g: the only constraint recorded is \"g(x) > -x\", which permits g(x)=a<0 at individual points. Hence \"V \u2286 {0,c}\" (and the exhaustive split S_0 \u222a S_c = R_{>0} used in \u00a76) does not follow. The needed lemma d(t) \u2265 0 for all t (rubric item S) is proved nowhere in the text; the objector's repair \u2014 iterating (4) gives g(x+na)=a and x+na>0 for all n, impossible for a<0 \u2014 is correct but absent. Since \u00a7\u00a74\u20137 rest on the two-value dichotomy, the necessity argument is incomplete as written."}
